originality.rationale: The claim is an exact classification of the least monoid congruence generated by binary two-letter palindromic duplications, with 19 classes and canonical representatives. The 2020 source proves code constructions via specially selected irreducible roots and exhibits nonunique palindromic roots; the 2023 source proves a zero-rate theorem for directed error correction. Neither inspected text gives or logically entails the statement-level congruence classification. Published-result semantic searches did not return a matching claim; this is limited evidence and not uniqueness proof.
residual_risks: A pre-existing congruence classification may be buried in rewriting-system or semi-Thue literature under different vocabulary, including unindexed work.
The exact optimal number of directed all-error palindromic-duplication codewords is not implied by the symmetric congruence classification.
The first-source publication date 2020-05-20 is used only for the related motivating literature and not as evidence that this new result appeared then.

value.rationale: An exact finite-index classification for the naturally motivated binary palindromic-duplication rewriting congruence closes a genuine all-words structural gap left by ambiguous roots and generic asymptotic capacity bounds. It gives canonical classes for arbitrarily long words, a minimal 19-element quotient, and a natural explicit eight-word all-error code construction in each length >=4. These are structural statements for a whole infinite family, not arbitrary finite census or routine restatement; no claim of optimal directed code size.
